subdivision_of_building: The proposal affects only a small portion of the external north/side elevation of the building at ground floor level, where a single air conditioning unit has been installed.
description:
This application seeks retrospective planning permission for the retention of an externally mounted air conditioning heat pump unit on the north/side elevation at ground floor level of the commercial retail premises.

The unit is mounted discreetly on the external wall and serves the interior climate control needs of the premises. The installation was undertaken to support comfortable working conditions and energy efficiency.

In terms of impact on the public realm, the air conditioning unit does not protrude excessively into the footpath. The distance from the installed unit to the road curb is approximately 205cm, which exceeds the clearance for nearby existing street furniture — namely a post box (142cm from wall) and a traffic sign post (180cm from wall) located on the same stretch of pavement. As such, the installation does not reduce pedestrian access or cause obstruction beyond what is already established by permanent public infrastructure.

Regarding noise and disturbance, the unit is a standard consumer-grade system that meets relevant operational standards. It operates within acceptable decibel levels for residential and commercial environments. Importantly, no complaints have been received from neighboring tenants or nearby residents since its installation, and the unit has not caused any measurable nuisance through noise or vibration.

There is no change of use proposed as part of this application. The property will continue to operate under its existing commercial use.
decision_conditions: The proposed air source heat pump, because of its size, location, and lack of evidence to demonstrate that there would be no adverse impacts on the amenities of the adjoining residential occupiers through noise, vibration, and general disturbance. As such, the proposed development is contrary to policy D14 (Noise) of The London Plan (2021), and policy LP2 (Development and Amenity) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).&nbsp;

<p>The proposed development, by reason of its size, design, materials, and positioning, would result in an obtrusive and incongruous form of development that represents poor quality design that fails to complement local (residential) character and is out of keeping with the appearance of the host building. As such, the proposal is contrary to policies D1 (London's form character and capacity for growth,&nbsp; D3 (Optimising site capacity through the design-led approach), D4 (Delivering good design) of The London Plan (2021) and policies PP1 (Public Realm), and LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020), and the guidance contained within Hackney's Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (2009).&nbsp;</p>

<p>The propsoed equipment, due to its size, positioning, and oversailing of the public footpath,<span style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px;"><span style="font-size:10pt;background-color:transparent">&nbsp;results</span></span><span style="background-color: transparent; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 10pt; white-space-collapse: preserve;">&nbsp;in an obstruction of the public pavement, affecting the free flow of pedestrian movement in this residential location, harming the pedestrian environment and the quality of the public realm. As such, the proposal is contrary to policies PP1 (Public Realm) and LP41 (Liveable Neighbourhoods) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020) and</span><span style="background-color: transparent; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 10pt; white-space-collapse: preserve;"> Section 177 of the Highways Act 1980. </span></p><span id="docs-internal-guid-4331cf45-7fff-3dc1-4944-b2abe73dfbe6"><div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;"><br></span></div></span>
